﻿# 在竞争激烈的市场中找到PMF

## 冷启动：MBA学生的第二次创业

Emma 是 MBA student。

Entrepreneur in residence at Chicago Ventures。

Gave herself two years personal runway to validate ideas。

Trial co-founder relationships。

Work in venture capital。

Last startup was developer marketplace called Moonlight。

Grew to $10K MRR with $55K monthly GMV。

Sold company to Google-backed startup PullRequest in 2020。

Now working on Velvet。

Velvet is AI gateway to run model analytics、evaluations、continuous monitoring。

Just at beginning of huge wave of AI adoption。

Becoming part of mainstream tech stack。

Velvet provides infrastructure to observe and control models in production。

Logged more than 60 million requests for startups building AI features using foundation models like OpenAI and Anthropic。

Hundreds of developers trust Velvet to run LLM operations。

Approaching six figures in revenue with mix of bottoms-up developer adoption and annual contracts sold to growth-stage startups。

## 反直觉：先有钱客户，才做产品

First product at Velvet was AI copilot。

Enabled text-to-SQL on top of any database。

Most customers used it to analyze LLM data from OpenAI and Anthropic。

Studied usage and began prototyping AI-specific tooling：

Request warehousing、caching、evaluations。

Just her and co-founder Chris for first year。

With occasional fractional engineer。

Once saw signals of real demand。

Brought on two founding engineers (Jack and Andy) to move faster。

Things accelerated quickly once had paying customer using in production。

Spring of 2024，one of customers requested access to AI gateway。

As heavy users of OpenAI's batch endpoint。

Needed granularly analyze cost、latency、other metrics。

Spent summer building proxy for them to warehouse request logs from OpenAI to PostgreSQL database。

Amazing design partner because had product-market fit。

Senior engineering team。

Strong opinions。

September，launched self-serve version of product。

Now any developer can sign up and start capturing logs in about five minutes。

Developers use platform to run model experiments、continuous monitoring、fine-tuning workflows。

## 暴击：筹款环境变了，要先有产品再拿钱

Finding product-market fit is extremely difficult。

Startup can either invent something to create new market。

Or compete in market already exists。

WorldWideWeb initiated new market of internet web browsers。

Mercury competed in well-established banking market。

Recommend reading Clayton Christensen's Innovator's Dilemma for anyone operating disruptive technology startup。

Thought leadership drives adoption。

Incumbent best practices don't apply。

Iterative failure required。

Demonstrating value of disruption takes time。

Yet-to-exist market cannot be analyzed by investors。

Raised money before having concrete product in-market。

Meant had 18 months to build product、find PMF、show customer traction。

Fundraising game changed while playing it。

After pandemic bull run of 2022。

Bar for getting to second round of funding extremely high。

For people starting new companies today。

Recommend developing product before raising money。

If do raise money，prioritize enough cash and personal runway。

Show meaningful traction in more risk-averse fundraising environment。

##  punchline：保持动量是唯一重要的事

Momentum is only thing that matters when building 0-1 startup。

Means constantly shipping features、talking to customers、communicating progress。

Writes weekly memo each Sunday。

Sends to team at 8 AM Monday morning。

Sets tone for week and keeps things moving。

Do daily standup in Slack。

Entire team meets for 30-minute work session each day。

Aim to ship new code every week。

Followed by sharing updates with customers via product newsletter。

Operating startup is overwhelming in every way。

If doesn't feel chaotic，likely not moving fast enough to disrupt incumbents。

Setting timelines、metrics、weekly routine creates culture of accountability。

Reason to keep moving forward together。
